author: Georg Friedrich Carl Müller
principal_sources_used: Personal examination; official Gutachten prepared during Sinclair's treason investigation
historical_contribution: First surviving medical assessment of Hölderlin
lasting_influence: Established the earliest surviving clinical description.
comments: Written for a legal inquiry, not therapeutic treatment. Describes unintelligible multilingual speech and rare dilucida intervalla.

author: J. H. F. von Autenrieth
diagnosis_or_interpretation: Manie als Nachkrankheit der Krätze ("mania as a secondary consequence of scabies")
principal_sources_used: Seven months of institutional observation; treatment records; prescription book; clinical notes
new_documentary_evidence: Yes – seven months of institutional observation
lasting_influence: Produced the first sustained medical record and treatment history.
comments: Diagnosis reflects early nineteenth-century medical theory linking suppressed skin disease to insanity.

author: Wilhelm Waiblinger
principal_sources_used: Personal visits, conversations, recollections, literary memoir
historical_contribution: Established the enduring literary image of Hölderlin's madness
lasting_influence: Created the enduring image of the "mad poet."
comments: Highly influential but now recognized as blending observation with literary construction.

author: Wilhelm Lange
principal_sources_used: Waiblinger's memoir; published letters; poems; nineteenth-century biographies
historical_contribution: First systematic psychiatric pathography (Hölderlin. Eine Pathographie)
lasting_influence: Converted Hölderlin into a modern psychiatric case history.
comments: Reinterprets literary and biographical evidence through Kraepelin's concept of dementia praecox; little or no original archival research.

author: Karl Jaspers
diagnosis_or_interpretation: Psychopathological interpretation within the schizophrenia tradition
historical_contribution: Gave the psychiatric interpretation major philosophical influence
comments: Accepted the underlying diagnostic framework while emphasizing phenomenological understanding.

author: Uwe Henrik Peters
principal_sources_used: Published editions of letters and poems; Müller's report; Autenrieth; Waiblinger; twentieth-century psychiatric literature
historical_contribution: Connected Hölderlin's language to Kraepelin's concept of schizophasia
comments: Compares historical descriptions with modern psychiatric symptomatology rather than introducing new historical evidence.

author: Pierre Bertaux
diagnosis_or_interpretation: Rejects schizophrenia as the primary explanation
principal_sources_used: Extensive archival research; correspondence; Sinclair documents; political history; legal records
historical_contribution: Major challenge to the psychiatric orthodoxy
lasting_influence: Reopened political, literary, and historical explanations.
comments: Argues that political history, biography, and archival evidence have been overshadowed by retrospective diagnosis.

author: Recent psychiatric literature
principal_sources_used: Earlier psychiatric literature; published biographies; selected letters; Müller report; Waiblinger
historical_contribution: Continues or refines twentieth-century psychiatric interpretation
lasting_influence: Extends twentieth-century psychiatric traditions using essentially the same documentary corpus.
comments: Often relies on inherited interpretations rather than substantially new documentary evidence.
